import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** show who has the document open and where their cursor is, updated
many times a second, without writing any of it to the app's log.

That is **presence**: each device says what it is doing now, every node keeps
the latest word from each device in memory and passes it to the others, and
clients follow the changes as a stream.
It is not app state: nothing is logged, sealed to disk or seen by your app's
code, and a node that restarts starts with an empty table.
Anything that must survive goes through a call.
The rules are in [Presence](/protocol/presence/); this page is how to use it.

## Publish this device's state

`POST /apps/{app}/presence { seq, state }`:

- `state` is hex, at most 4 KiB of bytes once decoded. What the bytes mean is
  up to your frontend (JSON of a cursor is common). `null`, or no `state`,
  retracts this device's entry.
- `seq` is a number that must grow with every new state of this device.
  The node keeps the highest `seq` it has seen and ignores an update with a
  lower one, because updates reach the nodes in any order.
  Use the clock in milliseconds (`Date.now()`), so a reloaded page, which
  forgets its counter, still moves forward.
- The **same `seq` and the same state again is a heartbeat**: it keeps the
  entry alive and changes nothing else. The same `seq` with a different state
  is ignored.
- The author is whoever the node authenticated: the account, and as the device,
  the session's passkey (or the API key). One person on two devices is two
  entries. Anyone the app's access admits may publish; an anonymous caller
  cannot (`401`).

With mero-js (`presenceState` turns bytes into the hex the route takes):

```ts
import { presenceState } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';

const encode = (v: unknown) => presenceState(new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(v)));

let seq = Date.now();
let state = encode({ cursor: 0 });

async function moveCursor(cursor: number) {
  seq = Math.max(seq + 1, Date.now());
  state = encode({ cursor });
  await client.apps.presencePublish({ app, seq, state });
}

// Stay present: an entry no one refreshes for 7 s is dropped.
const heartbeat = setInterval(() => client.apps.presencePublish({ app, seq, state }), 3000);

// Leave on purpose (a closed tab simply stops heartbeating).
async function leave() {
  clearInterval(heartbeat);
  await client.apps.presencePublish({ app, seq: seq + 1, state: presenceState(null) });
}
```

## Follow everyone else

`GET /apps/{app}/presence` answers `{ present: [{ account, device, state }] }`,
the devices present now on the node you ask (and so the whole cluster, give or
take an update in flight).
`GET /apps/{app}/presence/stream` is a server-sent event stream: one
`snapshot` event (the same list), then a `presence` event per change,
`{ account, device, state }`, with `state: null` when a device left or expired.

```ts
const decode = (hex: string) =>
  JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(Uint8Array.from(hex.match(/../g)!, (b) => parseInt(b, 16))));

const here = new Map<string, unknown>();               // `${account}/${device}` -> state
const stop = new AbortController();

for await (const event of client.presenceStream(app, stop.signal)) {
  const entries = event.kind === 'snapshot' ? (event.data as PresenceEntry[]) : [event.data as PresenceEntry];
  if (event.kind === 'snapshot') here.clear();
  for (const { account, device, state } of entries) {
    const key = `${account}/${device}`;
    if (state === null) here.delete(key);
    else here.set(key, decode(state));
  }
  render(here);
}
```

`PresenceEntry` is exported by mero-js. Skip your own entry by comparing
`account` with the signed-in account (`(await client.auth.me()).accountId`).

The other clients:

```python
client.apps.presence_publish(app=app_id, seq=1, state="7b7d")   # hex
print(client.apps.presence_get(app=app_id).to_dict()["present"])
for e in client.presence_stream(app_id, limit=10, timeout=5):   # snapshot first, then changes
    print(e["kind"], e["data"])
```

```bash
meroctl instance presence publish my-doc --seq 1 --state 7b7d   # no --state retracts
meroctl instance presence list my-doc
meroctl instance presence stream my-doc --limit 10
```

Rust: `client.apps().presence_publish(..)`, `presence_get(..)` and
`Client::presence_stream(app)`, which yields `(id, kind, data)`.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | What happens past it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State | 4 KiB of bytes (8,192 hex characters) | `400 BAD_STATE` (also for state that is not hex) |
| Expiry (`PRESENCE_TTL_MS`) | 7 s without a heartbeat, swept every second | the entry is dropped and streams see `state: null` |
| Entries per app (`MAX_AUTHORS_PER_APP`) | 512 devices | a new device evicts the one heard from longest ago |
| Event and presence streams per node (`MAX_EVENT_STREAMS`) | 4,096 | `429 RATE_LIMITED`: try another node or later |

The stream holds a short buffer per app (256 changes). A client too slow to
read it loses the changes it missed without a sign, so reconnect (a new
`snapshot`) when a view looks stale, and on any disconnect.

<Aside type="caution">
  Presence is best effort and unverified history: it is not in any log or
  receipt, and a node passes on what an authenticated device said. Use it for
  what is on screen now, never for a decision your app stores.
</Aside>
